title: "1. Choose an environment"
description: "Install the Python tools for your workflow and distinguish preparation from native execution."

The first choice is where each operation happens. A preparation computer builds
source inputs and a portable handoff. A solver host has the native executable,
license where required, and resources to run it. An analysis computer reads the
complete returned package. These may be the same machine, but installing a
Python extra does not install either solver.

Start with Python 3.12 or 3.13 and a fresh virtual environment. These lessons
describe the current SCGSim development source; the published version number
alone does not promise the same API. Use the source revision recorded by the
selected documentation build and the [matched public inputs](../examples.qmd#public-inputs).
For a development checkout, install that checkout rather than an older package:

```bash
git clone --branch develop https://github.com/OrPenStrike/scgsim.git
cd scgsim
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e '.[palace]'
```

If reproducing a particular documentation build, select its recorded source
revision in this clone before installing. Choose the extra for the actual work:

| Work on this computer | Installation from the matching checkout | What it supplies |
|---|---|---|
| Resolve and plot returned results | `pip install -e .` | SCGSim, NumPy and Plotly |
| Prepare Palace geometry/mesh/config | `pip install -e '.[palace]'` | GDSFactory 9.x, GDS reader and Gmsh |
| Prepare ordinary HFSS or Q3D; use Q2D | `pip install -e '.[aedt]'` | GDS reader and PyAEDT 1.3.0 |
| Prepare source-first AEDT Surface EPR | `pip install -e '.[aedt-epr]'` | AEDT dependencies plus GDSFactory 9.x and KLayout 0.30.x |
| Inspect solver-bound geometry | `pip install -e '.[visualization]'` | Mesh reader, image tools and PyVista; combine with the backend extra |

A visualization installation can be combined with a backend, for example
`pip install -e '.[palace,visualization]'`. Rendering needs a usable native
OpenGL/EGL context; an unavailable context is a rendering error, not a reason to
show invented geometry. The [preview contract](../geometry-preview.qmd) describes
which modes can be unavailable.

## Match the public PDK and kernel

The public component facts and executable notebooks belong to OrPen SC PDK.
Use its pinned source listed on the course map, and resolve OrPen and SCGSim
in the same environment. Their shared GDSFactory, kfactory and KLayout versions
must come from one dependency resolution rather than two independent installs.
For the public Palace source example, pass both sources to one pip resolution:

```bash
python -m pip install -e '.[palace]' 'orpen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk.git@35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9'
```

Change the SCGSim extra to the branch you need; keep the PDK revision matched to
this course. Select that environment's Python kernel in your notebook frontend. Notebook
frontend tooling is a user environment choice, not a SCGSim runtime API.

```python
from importlib.metadata import version
print(version("scgsim"))
```

This observes the installed distribution version. Keep the checkout revision
with your study notes too: two source checkpoints can expose different APIs
under a development version. A successful import establishes Python package
availability, not native solver availability or geometry correctness.

## Prepare the solver host separately

Palace handoffs require your real Palace executable or wrapper, its supported
native configuration and the site's launch environment. You supply executable,
resources and setup commands. SCGSim generates the selected local or Slurm
script; it does not install Palace or submit jobs during preparation.

AEDT execution targets AEDT **2024.2** with **PyAEDT 1.3.0** and an appropriate
license. The package's Python 3.13 support is separate from evidence for a
particular native AEDT run. The generated script owns one new Desktop session,
saves and releases it, then records the observed result. Reading results later
does not require opening Desktop.

You are ready to [author the shared Xmon snapshot](../tutorial-xmon-input.qmd).
For the ordinary CPW AEDT families, use the [CPW input branch](aedt-inputs.qmd).
If you already have a complete returned run, start at
[restart and resolve](returned-results.qmd).
